summary: Cuzco is a reworking of Java/Mask Trilogy where players place tiles to build a hex map of temples, houses, and terraces while bidding for turn order with a unique auction mechanism. It's a dense, elegant Kramer/Kiesling area-control and majority-scoring game where positioning and timing matter far more than luck.
praised: Clever turn-order auction where higher bids act later
High replayability due to map variability
Elegant production and layered rules that reward mastery
criticised: Steep learning curve and rules overhead for new players
Older-feeling design that some find fiddly compared to modern euros

interaction.kind: area majority and blocking via tile placement
interaction.detail: Players place tiles on a shared hex map, contesting adjacent territory and majority in shared regions (houses, temples, terraces); the turn-order auction directly determines who gets to react to whom. Almost the entire board is shared and contested, so nearly every placement affects opponents' options.

scoring.why: Points come from repeated area-majority scorings across provinces plus separate tallies for markets, temples, and buildings.
scoring.how_you_win: You place tiles and buildings to control the most territory in each color region when scoring rounds trigger, accumulating points from majorities, markets, and temples; most total points after the final scoring wins.
